results.title: CUergo: Neutral Posture Typing
results.snippet: This posture is achieved when the keyboard is below seated elbow height and the keyboard base is gently sloped away from the user so that the key tops are accessible to the hands in a neutral posture. In this position the arms, shoulders, neck and back can relax, especially during brief rest pauses.

results.title: Proper Wrist Posture for Typing: Guide & Solutions | Eureka Ergonomic
results.snippet: To maintain a functional relationship with the keyboard, the user often compensates by increasing the angle of wrist extension. According to OSHA eTools for Computer Workstations, the top of the monitor should be at or slightly below eye level. This alignment keeps the neck in a neutral position, which relaxes the trapezius muscles and allows the shoulders to drop, ultimately facilitating a more relaxed and neutral path for the nerves traveling down the arm to the wrist.

results.title: Proper Typing Posture: Correct Position & Ergonomic Guide
results.snippet: Ensure neutral wrist positioning: Wrists should not bend up, down, or sideways—keeping them level minimizes strain.

results.title: 9 Tips for Proper Typing Posture | Typing.com Blog
results.snippet: Maintain a neutral wrist position; try not to arch your wrists up too high. Keep wrists straight and fingers curved over the keys, with thumbs hanging near the spacebar. Your wrists should be floating above and parallel to the keyboard.

results.title: ergonomic-guidelines.pdf - Environmental Health & Safety
results.snippet: Position the keyboard approximately at elbow height. ... When using a mouse, trackball, or special keypads, place the wrist in a neutral position.
